subject: general
question: A milkman mixes water in pure blends milk and offers the mixture for sale at the original cost price of milk. If he mixes 0.75 liters of water in every 5.25 liters of milk and sells the entire mixture at the price of pure milk, what is his profit percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Water added = 0.75 L | Milk = 5.25 L | Total mixture = 6 L

Cost = price of 5.25 L | Revenue = price of 6 L (sold at milk price)

Profit % = (Water / Milk) × 100 = (0.75 / 5.25) × 100

= (75 / 525) × 100 = (1/7) × 100 = 100/7 ≈ 14.28%

**∴ The correct answer is 100/7% ≈ 14.28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pure milk = 5.25 L

Water mixed = 0.75 L

Total mixture = 5.25 + 0.75 = 6 L

Selling price = cost price of pure milk per litre

Water costs nothing ⇒ CP = cost of 5.25 L milk only

**Formula used:**

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

Profit % = (Volume of water ÷ Volume of milk) × 100

(Since water is free, extra revenue earned = price of water volume sold as milk)

 Total Mixture = 6 Litres Pure Milk = 5.25 L Cost Price Component Water 0.75 L 
• CP = Price of 5.25 L milk SP = Price of 6 L milk (sold at milk rate) Profit = Price of 0.75 L | Profit % = 0.75/5.25 × 100 = 100/7 % ≈ 14.28% 

**Calculations:**

Let cost price of milk = ₹1 per litre

⇒ CP of mixture = cost of milk only = 5.25 × 1 = ₹5.25

⇒ SP of mixture = 6 litres sold at ₹1 per litre = ₹6.00

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 6.00 − 5.25 = ₹0.75

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (0.75 ÷ 5.25) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (75 ÷ 525) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 7) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 100/7 ≈ 14.28%

**∴ The correct answer is 100/7% ≈ 14.28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer — General Profit Formula

When a dealer mixes a free adulterant (water) with a pure substance and sells at CP: Profit % = (Quantity of adulterant ÷ Quantity of pure substance) × 100. Here: 0.75/5.25 × 100 = 100/7%. This is the fastest direct formula — no need to assume price per litre.

Alternate Profit Formula Using Total Mixture

Profit % = (Adulterant ÷ Pure substance) × 100 = (Adulterant ÷ (Total − Adulterant)) × 100. Also: Profit % = (Total mixture ÷ Pure substance − 1) × 100 = (6/5.25 − 1) × 100 = (0.75/5.25) × 100 = 100/7%. Both give the same answer.

Selling Below or Above CP — Adulterant Problems

If dealer sells at x% below CP: Net profit % = (Adulterant/Pure × 100) − x%. If he sells at x% above CP: Net profit % = (Adulterant/Pure × 100) + x%. In this question he sells at exactly CP so profit comes only from the free water added.

Ratio and Alligation for Mixture Problems

Milk : Water = 5.25 : 0.75 = 7 : 1. This means in every 8 parts of mixture, 7 parts are milk and 1 part is water. Concentration of milk = 7/8 = 87.5%. Alligation is used when two ingredients of different costs are mixed — here water has zero cost making the calculation simpler.
